Restore reopened native scientific reads from the resolver-verified native package. Retain its decoded plan, admitted input, admission ledger and plain result as one checked snapshot. Reconstruct the native preparation/count/inspection context with library operations only; never execute or rescore a restored study. A shared dataset read context distinguishes archived scientific evidence from actual admission summaries, asset availability and verbatim source text. Raw CSV reads remain lazy, byte- and semantic-checked, and explicitly refuse if unavailable.

A local optional NativeArtifactSource capability takes the exact RunRef and explicit budget. Genuine absence/pruning and legacy storage permit the existing recomputation path, including older Bound references that predate native packed packages. Bound alone does not prove native storage existed. Present incomplete/corrupt native storage refuses, without silent fallback. ProjectSession validates the exact saved declaration, bounded index and stored closure; hosts use their existing FIFO callback seam without scheduler waits under a Java monitor.

Backend restoration has a typed loading value and a per-run coalesced supervised operation, distinct from scientific jobs. Concurrent readers share it; publication rechecks current scope/bindings, and release/cancellation completes waiting readers. No archive IO runs under the submission/document synchronization mutex. Local NativeReads waits on the exact restoration and races its own close. Restored provenance names the verified manifest byte address, preserving the separate canonical result digest and avoiding a stamped original-completion claim. Wire additions require the next compatible protocol version; previous pins and old refusal behavior stay protected.

This slice does not migrate the runner to StampedStudyResult, export empty-input archives, alter scientific results, or close broader S3.7/G1 acceptance. It makes existing saved native artifacts useful for actual reopened reads while preserving truthful legacy recomputation.
